text:
support_beth: FYI getting a customer escalation — multiple 503/timeouts hitting hosted inference in eu-west1 since ~09:10 UTC. SLO burn alert fired. customer says ~30% of requests fail, p99 latency up. forwarding logs.
alex_sre: Copy. Do we have the grafana link and any recent deploys?
support_beth: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted-infer/eu-west1-overview. No deploys in the last 2 hours (deploy-bot shows no activity). attaching a repro curl the customer sent:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-std-4k","input":"short"}' \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/infer

responses intermittently 503 or hang until client timeout.
maria_platform: Observability note — prefetch and proxy p99 spiked around 09:08 UTC. Prefetch queue depth metrics show backs up. Could be batcher backlog -> handshake timeouts. Query I'm running:

# logs: show 5xx by upstream and route
index=ingress source=proxy status>=500 | stats count by upstream_cluster, route, status

jordan_oncall: Traces are weird — sampling gap in the timeframe. I see many requests with only frontend span, no downstream spans. observability-bot: trace-coverage-drop alert 5823344612. Looks like many requests never reached the infer-worker or spans dropped.
alex_sre: Steps I'll take now: 1) check token cache and auth broker logs for rate rejects 2) check kv-cache thrash + memory pressure on proxy 3) quick patch to increase proxy connection timeout to avoid shedding.
alex_sre: Running quick log command: `kubectl -n hosted logs -l app=infer-proxy --since=15m | jq -r '.message' | grep "503" | head -40`
support_beth: Also customer mentioned they switched to a client that opens many short-lived connections (fire-and-forget). Could be handshake fanout + small request overhead.
maria_platform: I pulled kv-cache metrics: cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 55% at 09:07. Eviction rate spiked. That will amplify backend work and KV hot keys could be thrashing.
alex_sre: Good catch. If a hot key pattern caused repeated cache misses we can hit worker CPU and increase tail latency. If worker queue fills we get 5xx from proxy.
jordan_oncall: Quick mitigation options: a) enable short-term prefix caching fallback for that customer b) apply per-tenant conn rate-limit c) route to quantized-variant or smaller model to reduce worker CPU.
support_beth: Customer asked for workaround asap — we suggested retry with exponential backoff and persistent connections. They asked if we can flip something on our side to reduce errors.
alex_sre: I'm going to enable a temporary per-tenant soft-rate-limit (50 rps) for the affected tenant id, and enable fallback-route to quant-std model. Rolling change now via infra runbook.
deploy-bot: rollout start: infra/ratelimit/soft-tenant-limits v2 -> 3 instances (alex) 5823344623

deploy-bot: rollout success: 5823344630

alex_sre: Also increased proxy keepalive to 90s and bumped upstream connection timeout from 30s -> 45s (hotfix) 5823344635

observability-bot: SLO burn alert cleared at 09:16 UTC 5823344660. p99 latency trending down, 5xx fraction decreased in the last 3m.
maria_platform: Tracing still shows gaps — I enabled debug sampling on one proxy pod for 5m to capture full spans and see why downstream spans are missing. Running: `kubectl exec -n hosted -c proxy <pod> -- curl -XPOST http://localhost:2222/debug/sampling?rate=1.0`
jordan_oncall: For postmortem: gather the following — a) kv-cache eviction logs around 09:00-09:15 b) request distribution by tenant c) connection churn metrics and TLS handshake errors d) any auth-broker 429s or rate rejects.
support_beth: Noted. I'll file a support ticket update to customer with mitigation steps and ask them to move to keepalive connections. I'll also offer a short-term dedicated lane if they need SLA immediately.
alex_sre: Proposed long-term actions: 1) per-tenant circuit-breakers + adaptive backoff 2) hotspot key mitigation (sharding or smaller kv entries) 3) improve prefetch heuristics to avoid overfetching on cache miss storms 4) increase trace sampling during SLO burns automatically.
maria_platform: Adding an alert to detect rapid drop in cache hit rate (>=25% drop within 5m) and fanout of small connections (>=X new conn/s per tenant).
jordan_oncall: I'll own the follow-up doc and a short blameless incident note. tagging alex & maria for action items.
support_beth: Customer confirmed errors decreased after our rate-limit/pinning suggestion. Closing the escalation, will reopen if anything reoccurs. :relieved:

alex_sre: Thanks team. Please paste any relevant logs in the incident doc. Closing thread unless further updates.
